findings.title: Preserve the established `next_cursor` response field
findings.explanation: This serialization change removes `next_cursor` from every page response and emits an undocumented new `cursor` key instead. A client that reads `next_cursor` will receive no continuation value for both nonterminal and terminal pages, breaking pagination traversal and terminal-page detection. The same root cause covers the pagination-boundary and response-contract lanes.
findings.failurePath: A caller passes a Page with `next_cursor` set to a token (or None) to `serialize_page`; the serializer now returns `{items, cursor}`. Consumers expecting the prior `{items, next_cursor}` contract cannot find the continuation field.
